transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I’m here because… there’s been trouble with a contract I’m working on. Environmental modeling. I’m pretty sure some people involved have been tracking my revisions and putting errors into the datasets, like they’re trying to make it look like I can’t lead the work.

My wife says it’s probably just version-control mistakes. Some of the junior analysts say that too. But… I don’t think that explains all of it.
Can you tell me more about why you believe people are intentionally sabotaging your work? Have you noticed any specific actions or evidence that supports this belief?

It’s… mostly in the files. I’ll make revisions to the modeling data, and then later there are errors there that weren’t there before. Not just small things, things that make it look like I don’t know what I’m doing.

People say it’s version-control problems. My wife says that too, and some of the junior analysts. But it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like someone’s watching what I change and then putting those mistakes in after. I know how these datasets are supposed to behave.
Do you feel like there are other ways people are working against you outside of these file issues?

Not really outside of that, no. It’s mainly the contract files… the revisions I make, and then errors showing up after. That’s what feels intentional to me. My wife says it’s version-control, and the junior analysts say the same, but… I don’t think that covers it.
Do you feel like people are trying to undermine you in other areas of your life, or is this mainly happening at work with the contract files?

Mainly at work. With that contract.

I haven’t really… noticed it in other parts of my life. It’s the files, the revisions. I make changes, then errors show up later, and it feels like someone’s tracking what I’m doing and putting them there so I look like I can’t handle leading it. My wife and the junior analysts keep saying it’s version-control, but… I don’t buy that completely.
Have you ever had thoughts or beliefs that others don’t seem to understand or agree with, even when there’s no clear evidence to support them?

I suppose… yes. This thing with the contract files.

People keep telling me it’s just version-control mistakes, my wife says that, the junior analysts say it too. But I’m pretty sure someone’s tracking my revisions and putting errors into the datasets after I work on them. It doesn’t feel like an accident to me.
Have you considered that others might be right about the version-control explanation, even though you don’t fully agree with it?

I’ve considered it, yes. I’m not saying I haven’t.

But… it doesn’t really add up to me. The timing is too specific. I make revisions, then the errors show up after, and it feels like someone on that contract is tracking what I’m doing and planting them so it looks like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts keep saying version-control, but I don’t fully believe that.

Even though others have given you alternative explanations, like version-control issues, do you feel completely certain that someone is intentionally following your changes and sabotaging your work on purpose?

Completely certain… I don’t know if I’d say it that way.

But I’m pretty sure. It keeps happening after I make revisions, and then the datasets have errors. It feels like someone on that contract is following what I change and putting them in so I look like I can’t lead it. Even if people keep saying it’s version-control, I don’t really accept that.
Outside of the issue with your contract files, have you ever had any other unusual beliefs that other people don’t seem to share or understand?

Not really… no. Nothing I’d put in that same category.

It’s mostly this contract thing—the revisions, the dataset errors showing up after I work on them. People say it’s version-control, but I don’t buy that. Outside of that, I can’t think of anything else.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts about the contract files were so clear or proven that you believed others were deliberately refusing to see what was obvious?

Yes… I guess sometimes it feels that way.

I mean, when the errors show up right after my revisions, it seems pretty obvious to me that someone on that contract is tracking what I’m doing and putting them there. So when my wife or the junior analysts say it’s just version-control mistakes, it feels like they’re not really looking at what’s in front of them.

Even though people have looked at the files and told you it's likely version-control issues, do you still feel certain that the only explanation is that someone is intentionally tracking and sabotaging your work?

Yeah… I still think that’s what’s going on.

I know they keep saying version-control, but it doesn’t explain it to me. The errors show up after my revisions, and it feels like someone on that contract is tracking the changes and putting them there so I look incompetent.

Even though people have reviewed the files and explained that the issues could be due to version-control problems, have you felt that their explanations are completely wrong and that the only possible answer is that someone is deliberately sabotaging your work?

Yes. I mean… I know what they say about version-control, but to me that doesn’t fit.

The errors show up after I revise the datasets. It feels like someone on that environmental modeling contract is tracking what I do and putting those mistakes in there so it looks like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts don’t see it that way, but… I think they’re wrong.

Even though others have explained the errors as version-control problems and possibly shown you how that could happen, do you still believe that the only explanation is that someone is intentionally tracking and sabotaging your work?

Yes… I still think that’s what it is.

I know they keep saying it could be version-control, but it doesn’t feel like that to me. It feels like someone on that environmental modeling contract is watching my revisions and putting errors in the datasets so I look like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts don’t agree, but… I don’t think they’re seeing it.

Despite others showing you how version-control issues could explain the errors, do you still feel that the only possible explanation is that someone is intentionally tracking and sabotaging your work?

Yes. I know they showed me that, but… I don’t buy it.

It’s too pointed. My revisions get tracked, then the dataset has errors, and it makes me look like I can’t lead the work. My wife and the junior analysts can say it’s version-control, but I think someone on that contract is doing it on purpose.
